instruction: Add the following reference to the reference list: "Mellor, D. D., Sathyapalan, T., Kilpatrick, E. S., Beckett, S., & Atkin, S. L. (2010). High-cocoa polyphenol-rich chocolate improves HDL cholesterol in Type 2 diabetes patients. Diabetic Medicine, 27(11), 1318-1321. doi: 10.1111/j.1464-5491.2010.03108.x". Then, update the citation in the third paragraph where I cite chocolate's cardiovascular benefits to include this new reference using its reference number.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

reference_contains: Mellor, D. D., Sathyapalan, T., Kilpatrick, E. S., Beckett, S., & Atkin, S. L. (2010)

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding a new reference about chocolate and HDL cholesterol to the reference list (bringing total to 14 references) and adding a citation in the third paragraph about cardiovascular health. The evaluator checks: (1) at least 14 references exist, (2) the new reference containing 'Mellor, D. D., Sathyapalan, T.' is present in the reference list.

scoring_breakdown.0.7: New reference text found in reference list

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Incomplete verification coverage - instruction requires TWO steps but evaluator only checks ONE
The instruction explicitly requires: (1) Add reference to reference list AND (2) Update citation in third paragraph to include the new reference
The evaluator only verifies that the reference was added (checks min_references=14 and reference_contains), but does NOT verify that the citation was updated in the third paragraph
expected.rules.citation_checks is an empty dict {}, meaning no paragraph citation verification is performed
The getter CAN extract paragraph citations (paragraph_citations field), but the metric is not configured to check them
Without verifying the citation update, the evaluator cannot determine if the task was fully completed - a user could add the reference but forget to cite it
Minor: Weight inconsistency - scoring_breakdown says 0.7 for reference check but metric code uses 0.4 weight for reference_contains (though total scoring logic may differ)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add citation verification to expected.rules.citation_checks to verify the third paragraph contains the new reference citation
Need to identify which paragraph index corresponds to 'the third paragraph where I cite chocolate's cardiovascular benefits' in the actual document
Expected structure should be: "citation_checks": {"<paragraph_index>": [<list of expected citation numbers including new reference>]}
Alternatively, could verify that ANY paragraph's citations increased to include the new reference number (less precise but still validates the requirement)
Clarify and fix the weight inconsistency between scoring_breakdown and actual metric weights
